pictures.author: xorge
pictures.observations: Complete960x720 ordinary photo linked directly from mapped temple way. Two tall smooth segmented shafts with Corinthian capitals/short joining lintel, four broken shafts at different heights including tall uncapped rear shaft. Stone bases on rubble/earthen portico mound, fallen drums/cornice fragments and low ruin walls. Shafts are plain, not fluted. No complete roof or intact temple walls.

pictures.author: Kristiantos
pictures.observations: Complete960x640 low upward detail confirms plain worn drum shafts, Corinthian capitals and plain broken lintel. Caption identifies east-facing structure viewed from northeast; use approximate facing with mapped long axis. This is a detail angle, not an archaeological floor plan.

pictures.author: High Contrast
pictures.observations: Complete960x578 wide front view resolves approach/ground coverage: two capped columns/short joining lintel, four uneven broken shafts, low masonry/rubble-filled mound and fallen drum/cornice blocks. Earthen approach with low traces rather than a complete broad reconstructed stair. Museum behind toward northwest agrees with map context. Fine ruined-cella layout remains approximate from the mapped extent.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Standing Temple of Hercules at Amman: two tall plain segmented shafts with original simplified Corinthian leafy capitals and short broken lintel, four broken uncapped shafts at distinct heights, molded bases/local rubble footings. Low interrupted cella/perimeter masonry, occupied earthen portico mound/graded front approach and a few fallen drums/cornice fragments. Existing shared Corinthian capital/base geometry is adapted without its fluted shaft. No intact cella/roof, restored missing column rows, copied inscription/sculpture atlas or separate hand-of-Hercules artifact. Museum, Roman Temenos, watchtower, sculpture garden and surrounding city remain independent.
